ANCHORAGE-A house built from a modified water tank is be- ing completed in Beck, an Eskimo village on the lower Kuskokwim River

 The home is one of four experi- mental houses being planned and erected by the Arctic Research Center here in an attempt to find sanitary homes which can be made and heated at little cost by the Alaska natives.

 A model of a log house destined for construction at Beaver, Indian village on the Yukon which being relocated away from the rivers path, now sits in the laboratory of the research center.

 A bungalow type home is a year old in Napaskiak, an Eskimo village about five miles below Bethel on the KuSkOkWlm; and another has recently been com pleted at Aniak, about halfway between Bethel and McGrath.

 The experiments are being made so that if ever a housing program gets underway here the plans for the best type of housing will already have been made.

 Researchers here hope that in the round Eek house they have the answer to the principal prob lem that faces them: to find a house that will save heat so the residents will not have to spend so much time hunting driftwood and can use that time hunting for food.

"Happy Birthday To You" and it

the object of the surprise.

ing room.

happiness and many years of re-

tired from the Pullman Company

7.

as many useful gifts from his
friends, including fishing tackle,
shirts, etc., at the party high-
lighted with the traditionally de-
corated birthday cake, trimmed
with pink roses and inscribed
"Happy Birthday Dear Brother."

To help prevent Christmas tree
fires, the Safety Council offers
eight simple precautions:


1. Buy a fresh tree. Be wary of
trees sold as "fireproof". And don't
attempt to flameproof Christmas
trees with chemical solutions.


2. Keep your tree in a cold place
until ready to use it. Before set-
ting up the tree, saw off diagonally
at least an inch of trunk and place
base in water-containing holder.
Keep water reservoir filled.


3. Locate tree well away from
fireplace, radiators, television sets,
powerful lights and other sources
of heat.


4. Use only electric lights, and
be sure they bear the Underwriters
Laboratories label. Check wires
for defects and loose sockets be-
fore putting on tree.


5. Too many light circuits on one
outlet may overload house wiring
and blow a fuse. Reduce the load
if this happens, or connect part to
another circuit outlet. Never in-
crease size of fuse, or substitute
a penny for a blown fuse.


6. Be sure ends of metallic icicles
or other decorations do not dangle
into light sockets where they can
cause a short circuit and flash fire.


7. Do not operate electric trains
or other electrical toys, which may
spark under tree.


8. Take tree down when needles
start to fall. Dispose of old trees
in fire-safe areas outdoors—never
in furnaces, stoves or fireplaces,
because they burn with almost ex-
plosive violence.
